knowledge.q: What does "decontamination" mean in the SPD workflow?
options: Reducing bioburden so an item can be safely handled or further processed
The final sterilization step before storage
Wrapping an instrument set for the OR

knowledge.q: The term "bioburden" refers to:
options: The number of microorganisms on an item before sterilization
The weight limit of a sterilizer load
The chemical residue left by detergent
The expiration date of a sterile pack

knowledge.q: Which PPE is required when working in the decontamination area?
options: Fluid-resistant gown, gloves, mask, and eye protection
No PPE if instruments are pre-rinsed

knowledge.q: Why must eye protection be worn in decontamination?
options: To protect against splashes of contaminated fluid and aerosols
To keep hair out of the technician's face
Eye protection is optional in decontamination

knowledge.q: In SPD, the workflow always moves from:
options: Any direction as long as items are covered

knowledge.q: Why is the one-directional dirty-to-clean flow enforced?
options: To prevent recontamination of cleaned and sterilized items
To reduce the number of staff needed

knowledge.q: A single-use (disposable) device should be:
options: Used once and discarded, never reprocessed
Reprocessed if it still looks clean
Wiped and returned to the shelf

knowledge.q: Cross-contamination is best described as:
options: Transfer of contaminants from a soiled item or surface to a clean one

knowledge.q: When must hand hygiene be performed in SPD?
options: Before and after glove use and when moving between areas
Only at the start of the shift

knowledge.q: Gloves in SPD:
options: Do not replace hand hygiene and must be changed between tasks
Are only required in the sterile storage area

knowledge.q: Soiled instruments transported to decontamination must be:
options: Contained in a closed, leak-proof, labeled container or bag
Carried openly on a tray to save time
Left uncovered if going a short distance
Rinsed and placed directly on the clean side

knowledge.q: The biohazard label on a transport container indicates:
options: The contents are contaminated and require precautions
The set is ready for the OR
The container is clean and empty

knowledge.q: Proper attire in the clean assembly area includes:
options: Clean scrubs, hair covering, and no jewelry on the hands

knowledge.q: Why is hand and wrist jewelry prohibited during instrument processing?
options: It harbors microorganisms and can damage instruments or gloves
It is purely an appearance rule
It slows down typing on the workstation
Jewelry is permitted if cleaned daily

knowledge.q: Point-of-use treatment of soiled instruments helps to:
options: Keep soil moist so it does not dry and harden before cleaning
Sterilize the instruments at the bedside
Count the instruments for the OR

knowledge.q: If soil is allowed to dry on instruments, the result is:
options: Harder cleaning and higher risk of incomplete decontamination

knowledge.q: The correct order of instrument reprocessing is:
options: Inspection, then cleaning, then transport to OR

knowledge.q: Cleaning must always occur before sterilization because:
options: Sterilization cannot be assured on a soiled instrument
Sterilizers cannot reach high temperatures otherwise
It is only a documentation requirement

knowledge.q: A chemical indicator (CI) on a pack demonstrates that:
options: The pack was exposed to the sterilization process conditions
The pack is within its shelf life

knowledge.q: Which indicator type directly confirms microbial kill?
During assembly, instruments should be inspected for:
options: Nothing — inspection happens in the OR

knowledge.q: A hinged instrument is inspected in which position?
options: Opened so box locks and serrations can be checked

knowledge.q: Instrument lubricant ("milk") used in SPD is:
Why must only water-soluble lubricants be used?
options: Oil-based products block steam contact and prevent sterilization

knowledge.q: A count sheet (tray list) is used during assembly to:
options: Verify the correct instruments and quantities are in the set

knowledge.q: Heavy instruments in a tray should be placed:
options: On the bottom so they do not crush delicate items

knowledge.q: Enzymatic detergents are used because they:
options: Break down organic soil such as blood and protein

knowledge.q: Detergent must be dosed according to:
options: Manufacturer instructions for concentration and water temperature
The number of instruments by eye

knowledge.q: An ultrasonic cleaner removes soil primarily through:
Instruments placed in the ultrasonic should be:
Why must instruments be thoroughly dried before packaging?
options: Residual moisture can compromise sterilization and cause wet packs

knowledge.q: A "wet pack" found after sterilization should be:
options: Used if the outside is dry
Left to air dry then used

knowledge.q: The three parameters required for steam sterilization are:
If a sterilizer does not reach its required temperature, the load is:
options: Not sterile and must be reprocessed
Sterile if the time was long enough

knowledge.q: Under Spaulding classification, a "critical" item is one that:
options: Enters sterile tissue or the vascular system and must be sterile

knowledge.q: Which is an example of a Spaulding "critical" device?
options: A surgical forceps used in an open procedure

knowledge.q: Sterile storage areas must be:
options: Clean, dry, temperature/humidity controlled, and away from contamination

knowledge.q: Sterile packages on storage shelves should be:
options: Handled minimally and kept off the floor
Stored on the bottom shelf touching the floor

knowledge.q: A biological indicator (BI) contains:
options: Highly resistant bacterial spores to challenge the sterilizer

knowledge.q: How often should a BI be run in a steam sterilizer at minimum?
options: At least weekly, preferably daily, and every implant load

knowledge.q: A pre-vacuum (dynamic-air-removal) sterilizer differs from gravity in that it:
options: Actively removes air before steam to improve penetration

knowledge.q: A Bowie-Dick test checks a pre-vacuum sterilizer for:
options: Adequate air removal and steam penetration

knowledge.q: Event-related sterility means a package is considered sterile:
options: Until its integrity is compromised by an event (tear, wet, etc.)
Until a printed date regardless of condition

knowledge.q: A sterile package found with a small tear should be:
When loading a steam sterilizer, packs should be:
options: Spaced to allow steam circulation, not crammed together

knowledge.q: Basins and cups in a load are positioned:
options: On edge/tilted so condensate can drain

knowledge.q: An internal chemical indicator should be placed:
options: In the area of each pack considered most difficult for steam to reach
Only on the outside of the pack

knowledge.q: If an internal CI has not changed after a cycle, the pack should be:
options: Considered a process failure and not used
Used if the external tape changed
Sent to the OR with a note

knowledge.q: Immediate-use steam sterilization (IUSS) is intended for:
options: Urgently needed items that cannot be processed through normal cycles

knowledge.q: IUSS-processed items should be:
options: Used immediately and not stored for later use
Stored for up to a week

knowledge.q: Loaner instrument sets should arrive at the facility:
options: Early enough to be inspected, cleaned, and sterilized before use
Just before the case to save storage
Already sterile and ready for OR

knowledge.q: Loaner sets must be:
options: Decontaminated and sterilized on-site before the first use
Used directly from the vendor box

knowledge.q: A heat- and moisture-sensitive device is best sterilized by:
options: A low-temperature method (e.g., hydrogen peroxide or EtO)

knowledge.q: The sterilization method is selected based primarily on:
options: The device manufacturer's instructions for use (IFU)

knowledge.q: Load documentation should record:
options: Sterilizer ID, cycle, contents, operator, and monitoring results

knowledge.q: Lot/load tracking enables the facility to:
options: Identify and recall affected items if a failure is found

knowledge.q: Hydrogen peroxide gas plasma sterilization is unsuitable for:
options: Cellulose materials such as paper, linen, and gauze

knowledge.q: A key advantage of low-temperature sterilization is:
options: It processes heat- and moisture-sensitive devices
It is faster than all steam cycles

knowledge.q: Loads containing implants should be:
options: Monitored with a BI and quarantined until the result is read

knowledge.q: Releasing an implant before the BI result is read is acceptable:
options: Only in a documented emergency with physician notification

knowledge.q: If a sterilizer fails a BI, the facility should:
options: Quarantine and recall loads back to the last passing test
Take no action if CIs passed
Recall every load from the past year

knowledge.q: The purpose of a recall is to:
options: Retrieve potentially non-sterile items before patient use

knowledge.q: Sterilization records should be retained:
options: According to facility policy and regulatory requirements
They do not need to be retained

knowledge.q: Accurate documentation supports:
options: Traceability, recall capability, and quality review

knowledge.q: A quality management system in SPD primarily exists to:
options: Ensure consistent, monitored, and improvable processes

knowledge.q: Standard operating procedures (SOPs) provide:
options: Documented, repeatable steps so processes are consistent

knowledge.q: When a process failure is identified, the first step is to:
options: Contain the problem and prevent affected items from reaching patients

knowledge.q: A corrective action is intended to:
options: Eliminate the cause so the failure does not recur

knowledge.q: An internal audit in SPD is used to:
options: Verify practices conform to standards and find improvement areas

knowledge.q: Audit findings should be:
options: Documented and used to drive improvement

knowledge.q: AAMI ST79 is best described as:
options: A comprehensive guideline for steam sterilization in healthcare facilities

knowledge.q: Accrediting bodies (e.g., Joint Commission) expect SPD to:
options: Follow recognized standards and manufacturer IFUs

knowledge.q: A useful SPD quality metric is:
Tracking tray accuracy/error rates helps a department to:
Root cause analysis aims to identify:
options: The underlying reason a problem occurred, not just the symptom

knowledge.q: Asking "why" repeatedly during analysis helps to:
options: Move past symptoms toward the true cause

knowledge.q: Departmental policies should be:
options: Reviewed and updated on a defined schedule

knowledge.q: When manufacturer IFUs conflict with an old policy, the department should:
options: Update the policy to align with current validated IFUs

knowledge.q: Survey readiness in SPD is best maintained by:
options: Consistent daily compliance, not last-minute preparation

knowledge.q: Releasing an implant before the BI result is read is acceptable:
options: Only in a documented emergency with physician notification

knowledge.q: If a sterilizer fails a BI, the facility should:
options: Quarantine and recall loads back to the last passing test
Take no action if CIs passed
Recall every load from the past year

knowledge.q: The purpose of a recall is to:
options: Retrieve potentially non-sterile items before patient use

knowledge.q: Sterilization records should be retained:
options: According to facility policy and regulatory requirements
They do not need to be retained

knowledge.q: Accurate documentation supports:
options: Traceability, recall capability, and quality review

knowledge.q: A quality management system in SPD primarily exists to:
options: Ensure consistent, monitored, and improvable processes

knowledge.q: Standard operating procedures (SOPs) provide:
options: Documented, repeatable steps so processes are consistent

knowledge.q: When a process failure is identified, the first step is to:
options: Contain the problem and prevent affected items from reaching patients

knowledge.q: A corrective action is intended to:
options: Eliminate the cause so the failure does not recur

knowledge.q: An internal audit in SPD is used to:
options: Verify practices conform to standards and find improvement areas

knowledge.q: Audit findings should be:
options: Documented and used to drive improvement

knowledge.q: AAMI ST79 is best described as:
options: A comprehensive guideline for steam sterilization in healthcare facilities

knowledge.q: Accrediting bodies (e.g., Joint Commission) expect SPD to:
options: Follow recognized standards and manufacturer IFUs

knowledge.q: A useful SPD quality metric is:
Tracking tray accuracy/error rates helps a department to:
Root cause analysis aims to identify:
options: The underlying reason a problem occurred, not just the symptom

knowledge.q: Asking "why" repeatedly during analysis helps to:
options: Move past symptoms toward the true cause

knowledge.q: Departmental policies should be:
options: Reviewed and updated on a defined schedule

knowledge.q: When manufacturer IFUs conflict with an old policy, the department should:
options: Update the policy to align with current validated IFUs

knowledge.q: Survey readiness in SPD is best maintained by:
options: Consistent daily compliance, not last-minute preparation

knowledge.q: What does "decontamination" mean in the SPD workflow?
options: Reducing bioburden so an item can be safely handled or further processed
The final sterilization step before storage
Wrapping an instrument set for the OR

knowledge.q: The term "bioburden" refers to:
options: The number of microorganisms on an item before sterilization
The weight limit of a sterilizer load
The chemical residue left by detergent
The expiration date of a sterile pack

knowledge.q: Which PPE is required when working in the decontamination area?
options: Fluid-resistant gown, gloves, mask, and eye protection
No PPE if instruments are pre-rinsed

knowledge.q: Why must eye protection be worn in decontamination?
options: To protect against splashes of contaminated fluid and aerosols
To keep hair out of the technician's face
Eye protection is optional in decontamination

knowledge.q: In SPD, the workflow always moves from:
options: Any direction as long as items are covered

knowledge.q: Why is the one-directional dirty-to-clean flow enforced?
options: To prevent recontamination of cleaned and sterilized items
To reduce the number of staff needed

knowledge.q: A single-use (disposable) device should be:
options: Used once and discarded, never reprocessed
Reprocessed if it still looks clean
Wiped and returned to the shelf

knowledge.q: Cross-contamination is best described as:
options: Transfer of contaminants from a soiled item or surface to a clean one

knowledge.q: When must hand hygiene be performed in SPD?
options: Before and after glove use and when moving between areas
Only at the start of the shift

knowledge.q: Gloves in SPD:
options: Do not replace hand hygiene and must be changed between tasks
Are only required in the sterile storage area

knowledge.q: Soiled instruments transported to decontamination must be:
options: Contained in a closed, leak-proof, labeled container or bag
Carried openly on a tray to save time
Left uncovered if going a short distance
Rinsed and placed directly on the clean side

knowledge.q: The biohazard label on a transport container indicates:
options: The contents are contaminated and require precautions
The set is ready for the OR
The container is clean and empty

knowledge.q: Proper attire in the clean assembly area includes:
options: Clean scrubs, hair covering, and no jewelry on the hands

knowledge.q: Why is hand and wrist jewelry prohibited during instrument processing?
options: It harbors microorganisms and can damage instruments or gloves
It is purely an appearance rule
It slows down typing on the workstation
Jewelry is permitted if cleaned daily

knowledge.q: Point-of-use treatment of soiled instruments helps to:
options: Keep soil moist so it does not dry and harden before cleaning
Sterilize the instruments at the bedside
Count the instruments for the OR

knowledge.q: If soil is allowed to dry on instruments, the result is:
options: Harder cleaning and higher risk of incomplete decontamination

knowledge.q: The correct order of instrument reprocessing is:
options: Inspection, then cleaning, then transport to OR

knowledge.q: Cleaning must always occur before sterilization because:
options: Sterilization cannot be assured on a soiled instrument
Sterilizers cannot reach high temperatures otherwise
It is only a documentation requirement

knowledge.q: A chemical indicator (CI) on a pack demonstrates that:
options: The pack was exposed to the sterilization process conditions
The pack is within its shelf life

knowledge.q: Which indicator type directly confirms microbial kill?
During assembly, instruments should be inspected for:
options: Nothing — inspection happens in the OR

knowledge.q: A hinged instrument is inspected in which position?
options: Opened so box locks and serrations can be checked

knowledge.q: Instrument lubricant ("milk") used in SPD is:
Why must only water-soluble lubricants be used?
options: Oil-based products block steam contact and prevent sterilization

knowledge.q: A count sheet (tray list) is used during assembly to:
options: Verify the correct instruments and quantities are in the set

knowledge.q: Heavy instruments in a tray should be placed:
options: On the bottom so they do not crush delicate items

knowledge.q: Enzymatic detergents are used because they:
options: Break down organic soil such as blood and protein

knowledge.q: Detergent must be dosed according to:
options: Manufacturer instructions for concentration and water temperature
The number of instruments by eye

knowledge.q: An ultrasonic cleaner removes soil primarily through:
Instruments placed in the ultrasonic should be:
Why must instruments be thoroughly dried before packaging?
options: Residual moisture can compromise sterilization and cause wet packs

knowledge.q: A "wet pack" found after sterilization should be:
options: Used if the outside is dry
Left to air dry then used

knowledge.q: The three parameters required for steam sterilization are:
If a sterilizer does not reach its required temperature, the load is:
options: Not sterile and must be reprocessed
Sterile if the time was long enough

knowledge.q: Under Spaulding classification, a "critical" item is one that:
options: Enters sterile tissue or the vascular system and must be sterile

knowledge.q: Which is an example of a Spaulding "critical" device?
options: A surgical forceps used in an open procedure

knowledge.q: Sterile storage areas must be:
options: Clean, dry, temperature/humidity controlled, and away from contamination

knowledge.q: Sterile packages on storage shelves should be:
options: Handled minimally and kept off the floor
Stored on the bottom shelf touching the floor

knowledge.q: A biological indicator (BI) contains:
options: Highly resistant bacterial spores to challenge the sterilizer

knowledge.q: How often should a BI be run in a steam sterilizer at minimum?
options: At least weekly, preferably daily, and every implant load

knowledge.q: A pre-vacuum (dynamic-air-removal) sterilizer differs from gravity in that it:
options: Actively removes air before steam to improve penetration

knowledge.q: A Bowie-Dick test checks a pre-vacuum sterilizer for:
options: Adequate air removal and steam penetration

knowledge.q: Event-related sterility means a package is considered sterile:
options: Until its integrity is compromised by an event (tear, wet, etc.)
Until a printed date regardless of condition

knowledge.q: A sterile package found with a small tear should be:
When loading a steam sterilizer, packs should be:
options: Spaced to allow steam circulation, not crammed together

knowledge.q: Basins and cups in a load are positioned:
options: On edge/tilted so condensate can drain

knowledge.q: An internal chemical indicator should be placed:
options: In the area of each pack considered most difficult for steam to reach
Only on the outside of the pack

knowledge.q: If an internal CI has not changed after a cycle, the pack should be:
options: Considered a process failure and not used
Used if the external tape changed
Sent to the OR with a note

knowledge.q: Immediate-use steam sterilization (IUSS) is intended for:
options: Urgently needed items that cannot be processed through normal cycles

knowledge.q: IUSS-processed items should be:
options: Used immediately and not stored for later use
Stored for up to a week

knowledge.q: Loaner instrument sets should arrive at the facility:
options: Early enough to be inspected, cleaned, and sterilized before use
Just before the case to save storage
Already sterile and ready for OR

knowledge.q: Loaner sets must be:
options: Decontaminated and sterilized on-site before the first use
Used directly from the vendor box

knowledge.q: A heat- and moisture-sensitive device is best sterilized by:
options: A low-temperature method (e.g., hydrogen peroxide or EtO)

knowledge.q: The sterilization method is selected based primarily on:
options: The device manufacturer's instructions for use (IFU)

knowledge.q: Load documentation should record:
options: Sterilizer ID, cycle, contents, operator, and monitoring results

knowledge.q: Lot/load tracking enables the facility to:
options: Identify and recall affected items if a failure is found

knowledge.q: Hydrogen peroxide gas plasma sterilization is unsuitable for:
options: Cellulose materials such as paper, linen, and gauze

knowledge.q: A key advantage of low-temperature sterilization is:
options: It processes heat- and moisture-sensitive devices
It is faster than all steam cycles
